display.purpose: The single big number on a stat block. One per tile, centered.

headline.purpose: Lobby greeting and board panel title — names the screen you're on.

title.purpose: Panel headers throughout the game shell.

body.purpose: Default text, message bubbles, form content.

label.purpose: Label voice — names a region (section heads, felt zone labels). Uppercase, bold, tracked.

micro.purpose: Turn badge and phase stepper steps only.

shadows.name: recessed-tray
shadows.value: inset 0 2px 6px light-dark(rgb(70 62 40 / 0.12), rgb(0 0 0 / 0.4)), inset 0 -1px 0 light-dark(rgb(255 255 255 / 0.4), rgb(255 255 255 / 0.03))
shadows.purpose: A container pressed into the page — the lobby tray. Pairs with a 1px warm border.

shadows.name: raised-bar
shadows.purpose: An interactive row lifted off a recessed tray — lobby game bars, reused for melds on the felt.

shadows.name: card-lift
shadows.purpose: The playing card's own shadow. A filter, not a box-shadow, so it follows the rounded silhouette.

shadows.name: panel-inset
shadows.purpose: The deep inner shadow on a panel body, marking it as the well inside its header.

shadows.name: ambient-small
shadows.purpose: Felt zones and feed bubbles resting on their background.

motion.name: card-transition
motion.value: transform 0.2s ease-in-out, filter 0.2s ease-in-out, background-color 0.2s ease-in-out
motion.purpose: Card select/deselect, hover lift, and face swap. Shared by the lock badge so it travels with the card.

motion.name: popup-slide
motion.purpose: Transient warning popup dropping in from the top of the viewport.

motion.name: card-hover-lift
motion.purpose: The reserved lift distance. Space is padded in advance so a raised card is never clipped.

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: The solid coral CTA. Hover and active dim the same hue rather than shifting it.
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { background-color: hsl(16 85% 62%); color: #fff; box-shadow: inset 0 0 0 1.8px hsl(16 85% 62%); border: none; border-radius: 4px; padding: 8px 16px; font-family: 'Noto Sans', sans-serif; font-size: 16px; font-weight: 600; cursor: pointer; transition: filter 0.2s ease-in-out; } .ds-btn-primary:hover { filter: brightness(0.94); } .ds-btn-primary:active { filter: brightness(0.88); } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid hsl(16 85% 62%); outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: CTA — View
components.description: The lobby's primary row action: solid coral. Shares a min-width with Join and Full so rows stay aligned.
components.css: .ds-cta { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; min-width: 4.5rem; padding: 8px 12px; border: 1.8px solid transparent; border-radius: 8px; font-family: 'Noto Sans', sans-serif; font-size: 14px; font-weight: 600; text-decoration: none; cursor: pointer; } .ds-cta-view { background-color: hsl(16 85% 62%); border-color: hsl(16 85% 62%); color: #fff; font-weight: 700; transition: filter 0.2s ease-in-out; } .ds-cta-view:hover { filter: brightness(0.94); } .ds-cta-view:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid hsl(16 85% 62%); outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: CTA — Join
components.description: Secondary row action: coral tint with a coral outline and coral-deep ink.
components.css: .ds-cta { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; min-width: 4.5rem; padding: 8px 12px; border: 1.8px solid transparent; border-radius: 8px; font-family: 'Noto Sans', sans-serif; font-size: 14px; font-weight: 600; text-decoration: none; cursor: pointer; } .ds-cta-join { background-color: color-mix(in srgb, hsl(16 85% 62%) 20%, light-dark(hsl(49 14% 100%), hsl(49 14% 8%))); border-color: hsl(16 85% 62%); color: light-dark(hsl(16 90% 42%), hsl(16 85% 62%)); transition: filter 0.2s ease-in-out; } .ds-cta-join:hover { filter: brightness(0.97); } .ds-cta-join:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid hsl(16 85% 62%); outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: CTA — Full
components.description: Deliberately inert: a muted chip that occupies the CTA slot when a game has no room. Not a disabled button.
components.css: .ds-cta { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; min-width: 4.5rem; padding: 8px 12px; border: 1.8px solid transparent; border-radius: 8px; font-family: 'Noto Sans', sans-serif; font-size: 14px; font-weight: 600; text-decoration: none; } .ds-cta-full { background-color: transparent; border-color: light-dark(hsl(49 14% 90%), hsl(49 14% 18%)); color: light-dark(hsl(49 14% 24%), hsl(49 14% 52%)); cursor: default; }

components.name: Turn Badge
components.description: The canonical 'it's your turn' object: coral-tint pill, coral outline, micro uppercase label, currentColor dot.
components.css: .ds-turn-badge { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 2px; padding: 2px 8px; border: 1.8px solid hsl(16 85% 62%); border-radius: 9999px; background-color: color-mix(in srgb, hsl(16 85% 62%) 20%, light-dark(hsl(49 14% 100%), hsl(49 14% 8%))); color: light-dark(hsl(16 90% 42%), hsl(16 85% 62%)); font-family: 'Noto Sans', sans-serif; font-size: 10px; font-weight: 700; text-transform: uppercase; letter-spacing: 0.03em; } .ds-turn-dot { width: 0.45em; height: 0.45em; border-radius: 9999px; background-color: currentColor; }

components.name: Game Bar on Tray
components.description: The signature elevation pair: a recessed warm-neutral tray holding a raised Lobby Slate bar. The shadows only work as a set.
components.html:
Friday Night
Crazy Eights
3/4View
components.css: .ds-tray { padding: 16px 20px; border-radius: 20px; background-color: light-dark(hsl(49 14% 98%), hsl(49 14% 10%)); border: 1px solid light-dark(rgb(90 80 55 / 0.14), rgb(200 185 140 / 0.09)); box-shadow: inset 0 2px 6px light-dark(rgb(70 62 40 / 0.12), rgb(0 0 0 / 0.4)), inset 0 -1px 0 light-dark(rgb(255 255 255 / 0.4), rgb(255 255 255 / 0.03)); } .ds-game-bar { display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: space-between; gap: 16px; padding: 12px 16px; border-radius: 12px; background-color: light-dark(#eef1f5, #262b32); box-shadow: inset 0 1px 0 light-dark(rgb(255 255 255 / 0.7), rgb(255 255 255 / 0.05)), 0 2px 7px light-dark(rgb(70 62 40 / 0.13), rgb(0 0 0 / 0.34)); font-family: 'Noto Sans', sans-serif; color: light-dark(hsl(49 14% 0%), hsl(49 14% 100%)); } .ds-game-bar-name { font-size: 16px; font-weight: 600; } .ds-game-bar-type { margin-top: 2px; font-size: 14px; color: light-dark(hsl(49 14% 24%), hsl(49 14% 52%)); } .ds-game-bar-meta { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 16px; white-space: nowrap; } .ds-game-bar-count { font-size: 14px; font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; color: light-dark(hsl(49 14% 24%), hsl(49 14% 52%)); } .ds-cta { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; min-width: 4.5rem; padding: 8px 12px; border: 1.8px solid hsl(16 85% 62%); border-radius: 8px; font-size: 14px; font-weight: 700; text-decoration: none; } .ds-cta-view { background-color: hsl(16 85% 62%); color: #fff; }

components.name: Selectable Playing Card
components.description: The card face is a real element (5/7 div with neutral fill and a drop-shadow filter); only rank/suit ink is an image. Selection is a visually-hidden real checkbox labelled by the whole card.
components.css: .ds-hand-card { position: relative; display: inline-block; width: 80px; cursor: pointer; font-family: 'Noto Sans', sans-serif; } .ds-hand-input { position: absolute; width: 1px; height: 1px; margin: -1px; padding: 0; overflow: hidden; clip: rect(0,0,0,0); border: 0; } .ds-playing-card { display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; width: 100%; aspect-ratio: 5 / 7; background-color: light-dark(hsl(49 14% 90%), hsl(49 14% 18%)); border: 1.8px solid light-dark(hsl(49 14% 90%), hsl(49 14% 18%)); border-radius: 4px; filter: drop-shadow(0 3px 4px rgb(0 0 0 / 0.6)); transition: transform 0.2s ease-in-out, filter 0.2s ease-in-out, background-color 0.2s ease-in-out; } .ds-card-ink { font-size: 18px; font-weight: 600; color: light-dark(hsl(49 14% 20%), hsl(49 14% 80%)); } .ds-hand-input:enabled ~ .ds-playing-card { outline: 2px solid light-dark(hsl(49 14% 55%), hsl(49 14% 45%)); outline-offset: -2px; } .ds-hand-input:focus-visible ~ .ds-playing-card { outline-color: light-dark(hsl(49 14% 28%), hsl(49 14% 44%)); background-color: light-dark(hsl(49 14% 70%), hsl(49 14% 24%)); } .ds-hand-input:checked ~ .ds-playing-card { transform: translateY(-20px); background-color: hsl(16 45% 20%); outline: 2px solid hsl(16 85% 62%); outline-offset: -2px; } .ds-hand-input:checked ~ .ds-playing-card .ds-card-ink { color: hsl(49 14% 92%); } .ds-lock { position: absolute; top: 8px; right: 8px; z-index: 1; color: hsl(16 85% 62%); font-size: 14px; pointer-events: none; transition: transform 0.2s ease-in-out; } .ds-hand-input:checked ~ .ds-lock { transform: translateY(-20px); }

components.name: Felt Zone
components.description: A brighter panel laid on the green felt. Green exists only inside this zone — never on chrome.
components.html:
Melds
Shared melds go here
components.css: .ds-felt { padding: 16px; border-radius: 20px; background-color: light-dark(#bfd2c6, #1b2a22); font-family: 'Noto Sans', sans-serif; } .ds-felt-zone { display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 12px; padding: 12px 16px; border-radius: 12px; background-color: light-dark(#e6f5ea, #274035); box-shadow: 0 1px 2px hsl(0deg 0% 0% / 3%), 0 2px 6px hsl(0deg 0% 0% / 15%); color: light-dark(hsl(49 14% 0%), hsl(49 14% 100%)); } .ds-felt-label { font-size: 12px; font-weight: 700; text-transform: uppercase; letter-spacing: 0.04rem; color: light-dark(hsl(49 14% 24%), hsl(49 14% 52%)); } .ds-felt-body { font-size: 14px; }

components.name: Feed Bubble Stack
components.description: Rummy's floating message trail. Age reads as opacity (0.6 fading, 0.3 ghost); the directive bubble inverts to solid coral and there is never more than one.
components.html:
Ana drew from the deck
You melded 7♠ 7♥ 7♣
Ana discarded K♦
Discard to end your turn
components.css: .ds-bubble-stack { display: flex; flex-direction: column; align-items: flex-end; gap: 4px; width: 260px; font-family: 'Noto Sans', sans-serif; } .ds-bubble { max-width: 100%; padding: 12px 16px; border-radius: 12px 12px 4px 12px; font-size: 14px; background-color: light-dark(hsl(49 14% 100%), hsl(49 14% 8%)); color: light-dark(hsl(49 14% 0%), hsl(49 14% 100%)); border: 1.8px solid light-dark(hsl(49 14% 90%), hsl(49 14% 18%)); box-shadow: 0 1px 2px hsl(0deg 0% 0% / 3%), 0 2px 6px hsl(0deg 0% 0% / 15%); } .ds-bubble-ghost { opacity: 0.3; } .ds-bubble-fade { opacity: 0.6; } .ds-bubble-directive { background-color: hsl(16 85% 62%); border-color: hsl(16 85% 62%); color: #fff; font-weight: 700; } .ds-bubble-directive::before { content: '\279C'; margin-right: 2px; }

components.name: Panel
components.description: The game shell's building block: a raised-chrome header with a hairline bottom border over an inset well.
components.css: .ds-panel { display: flex; flex-direction: column; font-family: 'Noto Sans', sans-serif; color: light-dark(hsl(49 14% 34%), hsl(49 14% 54%)); border-radius: 8px; overflow: hidden; } .ds-panel-header { display: flex; align-items: center; padding: 12px 16px; background-color: light-dark(hsl(49 14% 98%), hsl(49 14% 10%)); border-bottom: 1.8px solid light-dark(hsl(49 14% 90%), hsl(49 14% 18%)); } .ds-panel-header h2 { margin: 0; font-size: 18px; font-weight: 600; color: light-dark(hsl(49 14% 0%), hsl(49 14% 100%)); } .ds-panel-body { flex: 1; padding: 16px; font-size: 14px; background-color: light-dark(hsl(49 14% 100%), hsl(49 14% 8%)); box-shadow: inset 0 8px 12px hsl(0deg 0% 0% / 15%), inset 0 4px 4px hsl(0deg 0% 0% / 3%); }

narrative.overview:
A lamp-lit room in a warm house, late in the evening — and the lights are low. This is a dark-first system: dark is the scheme that gets designed and judged. The chrome is the room itself, a yellow-tinged linen gray that never announces itself, because it is walls and furniture, not the event. Coral is the single lit signal in that room, everywhere in the house: it means act — your turn, this button, this link, this name. Nothing else glows.

Each major room may be its own color. Coral is the constant, site-wide; on top of it, a major page may claim one accent of its own so that arriving there feels like arriving somewhere. The game page claimed green and became a felt table. The games index claimed a cool slate and became the hallway. Neither color is allowed anywhere else, and neither is the whole list — the next page that earns one picks its own. Pages that don't claim a color are not unfinished; warm chrome plus coral is a complete page.

The room is physical, not flat. Trays are recessed into surfaces and bars sit raised on top of them; cards cast real shadows and lift when you touch them; the felt has brighter panels laid over it. Depth here is literal furniture logic, not decoration — if two things are stacked, the stack is visible. Density is comfortable rather than compressed: this is a room you spend an evening in, not a dashboard you scan.

The system's one hard discipline is color scarcity. Optics supplies neutral chrome and every non-color measurement; color is never derived from a ramp. One brand accent, at most one page accent per page, and nothing else. A screen with coral in three unrelated places, or with a second page's color bleeding into it, has broken the world.
keyCharacteristics: Dark-first: dark is the designed scheme; light mode is not yet a designed surface
Warm linen-gray chrome (hue 49°) that reads as room, not as UI
One permanent coral accent (hue 16°), site-wide, reserved for action, turn, and identity
Page accents: a major page may claim one color of its own, and it never leaves that page
Literal, stacked depth: recessed trays, raised bars, drop-shadowed cards
Cards are real elements with real stock, not images
Comfortable density on a desktop-first canvas

rules.name: The No-Ramp Rule
rules.body: Never color a component from Optics' primary ramp (--op-color-primary-*). Its lightness knob is inert and its base is locked mid-dark in both schemes, so it cannot reach a bright hand-picked accent. Optics owns neutrals and non-color tokens; every actual color is hand-picked. The primary hue is pointed at coral for one reason only — so Optics' own internal chrome (focus rings, focused inputs) reads coral instead of a stray default.

rules.name: The One Page, One Color Rule
rules.body: A major page may claim exactly one accent of its own, and that color may not appear on any other page. One is the ceiling, not the target: pages with no accent are complete. Where the color lands within the page — the stage, the rows, a single surface — is that page's own call and is deliberately not systematized. If a page color shows up in shared chrome or on a second page, it has leaked; remove it rather than spreading it further.

rules.name: The One Signal Rule
rules.body: Coral means 'act.' Turn state, primary actions, links, focus, and brand identity — nothing else, on every page. A page accent never takes over an action, and coral never becomes a page's decoration. A screen where coral also decorates a heading, a border, and a divider has spent the signal.

rules.name: The Dark-First Rule
rules.body: Dark is the designed scheme. Author, review, and screenshot in dark mode; that is what 'correct' means here. Light mode is currently incidental output from Optics' light-dark() pairs, so a light-mode oddity is a known state, not a bug worth chasing — a hand-picked light palette is planned and will replace the dynamic switching with explicit values. Until then, don't tune light values, and don't block on them.

rules.name: The Pair Rule
rules.body: Even though only dark is designed, keep every color a light-dark() pair or an Optics pair — never substitute a raw hex for one. Hard-coding a fixed color both breaks light mode outright and forfeits the seam the future light palette will be written into. Note that Optics' plus-N steps trade direction between schemes (a lower number is darker in light mode but lighter in dark mode, Material-style elevation), so 'one step darker' is not one thing — pick the step that's right in dark, and let light fall where it falls.

rules.name: The Label Voice Rule
rules.body: Uppercase + bold + letter-spacing is reserved for naming a region (section heads, felt zone labels, scoreboard columns, status chips). Never use it for a sentence, a button, or body copy.

rules.name: The Tabular Rule
rules.body: Any figure that updates live — card counts, player counts, stats — gets font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums. Digits changing width mid-game reads as jitter.

rules.name: The Definite Height Rule
rules.body: Card sizing cascades down from a definite height, not up from content. .hand-wrap establishes the band, .hand-fan fills it, .hand-card carries height: 100%, and the card resolves its width from aspect-ratio: 5 / 7. Rummy's hand panel is capped to clamp(140px, 22vh, 220px) plus the hover-lift allowance for exactly this reason. Break the chain and cards collapse.

rules.name: The Reserved Lift Rule
rules.body: Wherever a card can lift, the room for the lift is reserved in advance — .hand-fan pads its top by the lift distance (50px) so a raised card isn't clipped by its own scroll container.

rules.name: The Matched-Pair Rule
rules.body: Recessed and raised shadows ship together. A raised bar with no recessed tray beneath it, or a tray with flat children, loses the entire effect.

rules.name: The Filter-Not-Box Rule
rules.body: Card shadows use filter: drop-shadow(...). Cards are rounded, occasionally rotated, and layered — a box-shadow would trace the wrong outline.

rules.name: The Radius-Tracks-Size Rule
rules.body: Pick radius by surface scale, not by taste: chip 2–4px, control 8px, container 12px, stage 20px. A 20px radius on a small chip reads as a lozenge; a 4px radius on the felt reads as a bug.

rules.name: The One Aspect Rule
rules.body: Every card representation is 5 / 7, at every scale. Never free-size a card.

dos: Do take every surface, border, and body-text color from the Optics neutral scale, and every non-color value (spacing, type, radius, shadow) from an --op-* token.
Do hand-pick color as a project token: --gf-color-accent* for coral, --gf-felt* for the game page, --gf-lobby-bar for the games index.
Do use Accent Coral Deep whenever coral is text and Accent Coral whenever coral is a fill. The deep pair is the one that stays legible on either page background.
Do design, review, and screenshot in dark mode — that is the scheme that counts.
Do keep colors as light-dark() pairs anyway, so the future light palette has a seam to be written into.
Do give a new page its own accent when it genuinely benefits from feeling like its own place — and put it wherever suits that page.
Do pair recessed and raised shadows as a set.
Do give every card representation the 5 / 7 ratio, at every scale.
Do use filter: drop-shadow() for card shadows and box-shadow for boxes.
Do reserve space for a lift before animating one.
Do put live-updating numerals in tabular-nums.
Do dim coral with a brightness() filter for hover and active states.
Do keep one BEM block per file, elements and modifiers nested under the block.
donts: Don't color anything from --op-color-primary-*. The ramp cannot reach this coral, and the primary hue is pointed at coral only for Optics' internal chrome.
Don't let a page's accent appear on another page: green belongs to the game page, Lobby Slate to the games index, and neither belongs in shared chrome.
Don't give one page two accents, and don't assign a color to stats, history, or rules just to complete the pattern — no accent is a finished state.
Don't spend coral on decoration. If it isn't action, turn state, focus, or brand, it isn't coral. And never let a page accent take over a coral job.
Don't treat a light-mode oddity as a bug to fix today. Light is undesigned until it gets its hand-picked palette.
Don't substitute a raw hex for an Optics plus-N/minus-N token — those are light-dark() pairs, and hard-coding one forfeits the seam the light palette needs.

Don't wrap a full shadow or border shorthand in light-dark(). It accepts two <color> arguments only; a shorthand silently invalidates the whole declaration to none with no console warning. Wrap only the color portion of each layer.
Don't derive a coral ramp. Coral is a few chosen shades at 16°; a generated ramp drifts toward muddy copper.
Don't fade a disabled card with opacity — darken its face instead, so the ink stays true.
Don't replace the hidden-checkbox card selection with a click handler on a div.
Don't port one game's hand-overflow strategy to another. Go Fish and Crazy Eights overlap and never scroll; Rummy scrolls and never overlaps. Both choices are load-bearing.
Don't reference a --_gf-* private token from outside its own component file.
Don't use label voice (uppercase + bold + tracking) for anything but naming a region.
